AddApplicationNoteRequest.description:
A note from the hiring team on an application, kept on its timeline with the author and the time. Mention a member
as `@[userId]`: they get a notification and an email that never quotes the note.

AddApplicationTagRequest.description: A tag to add to an application. Tags compare ignoring case; conditions read them as `application.tags`.

AddedFromTalentPool.description:
The new applications, one per candidate added, and how many were skipped because they had already applied to the
job. Each new application carries the candidate's permission for future roles from the one they were kept from.

AddFromTalentPoolRequest.description: Adds these saved candidates to `jobId`, which must not be closed.

AddVerificationNoteRequest.description: Adds a note to the verification audit log, about one assessment (`assessmentId`) or the application as a whole.

AiAssistanceAssessmentView.description: How much of the content appears generated or templated? Informational, and relative to the job's AI policy.

AiAssistanceLevel.description: AI assistance levels, lowest first. Informational and relative to the job's AI policy.

AiCostBasis.description: Where a call's cost came from.

AiKeySource.description: Whose key paid for a call.

AiPolicyContext.description: Where the candidate's AI use stands against the job's policy, from the policy and the declaration only.

AiUsageCallPage.description: A page of calls, newest first. `nextBefore` is the id to pass as `before` for the next page, null on the last.

AiUsageCallView.description:
One model call, as it happened. `providerRequestId` is the provider's id for the response, which finds the call in the
provider's own logs. Tokens are null when the provider reported none. `cost` is null when `costBasis` is
`Unknown`. `check` names the check (for example `consistency.extraction`). Holds nothing that was sent or received.

AiUsageDay.description: One day of use, by the date in the requested time zone (`yyyy-MM-dd`).

AiUsageGroup.description: Use by one provider, model and key source.

AiUsageLimitsView.description:
The organization's monthly AI budget (alerts at 50%, 80% and 100%, stops nothing) and cap (pauses the AI-based checks), in
one `unit`. `budget` and `cap` are what the organization set; `effectiveBudget` and `effectiveCap` are
what applies, which for ScreenHire's key falls back to the deployment's defaults, in tokens. An own key has no default.

AiUsageLimitView.description:
One monthly limit in force. `amount` is in `unit`; `isDefault` says it is the deployment's default for
ScreenHire's key, not one the organization set; `used` is this month's use in the same unit; `percent` is how far
that is, whole percent, and can pass 100 (the cap is checked before each check, so a check in flight can pass it).

AiUsageSummary.description:
This organization's AI use between `from` and `to` (default: this month, UTC). Totals count calls; `callsWithUnknownCost`
are calls nothing could price, which count as no cost. Days are the requester's days (`timeZone`). `limits` is
the month's position against the budget and cap, whatever range was asked for.

AiUsageTotals.description: Calls, tokens and cost over a range. `cost` is in US dollars and counts only calls with a known cost.

AiUseDeclaration.description: The candidate's answer to "did you use AI tools to apply?".

AiUsePolicy.description: What the employer allows candidates to do with AI tools while applying.

AnswerFact.description: A candidate's answer to one question. A multiple-choice answer has one value per chosen option.

ApiKeyScope.description: What an API key may do on the hiring API.

ApiKeySummary.description:
An organization API key as listed: never the key itself, which only CreatedApiKey carries.
`prefix` is the key's first characters. `permitsPerMinute` is null for the deployment's default.
`lastUsedAt` is accurate to about a minute. `createdByUserId` is the member who created it, or null once their
account is deleted; removing a member offers to revoke the keys they created.

ApiMeta.description:
What is serving this API: the product name, the build version, the hosting environment, and the API's public origin
(`ScreenHire:Domains:ApiHost`), which the API reference (`/scalar`), the OpenAPI file and `/v1` sit under.
`careersUrlPattern` is a tenant's careers address with `{tenant}` where its slug goes, such as
`https://{tenant}.careers.example.com` (`ScreenHire:Domains:CareersHostPattern`), so the dashboard can show the
address a name will get.

ApplicationAnswer.description:
One answer to a screening question, in the form automation conditions read (`answers.{QuestionId}`):
`yes` or `no` for yes/no questions, an option id for single choice, the text, number or URL for the
others, and an upload id for a file question. Multiple choice answers are option ids in `values`.

ApplicationDetail.description:
One application: the candidate, the job, where it is in the job's workflow, its tags, the candidate's
declarations, answers and files.

ApplicationEmailDraft.description: Wording for one email, rendered with the candidate of `applicationId`, before a person sends it.

ApplicationFileSummary.description: A file the candidate uploaded. `scanStatus` is the malware scan's result; `NotScanned` means no scanner is configured.

ApplicationInterview.description:
An interview offered to the candidate. `status` is `Open` (waiting for the candidate to pick a time),
`Booked`, `Cancelled` or `Expired` (the window passed with no booking; an Open request past its window
reads as Expired). `startsAt` and `endsAt` are set once booked, and stay on a cancelled interview that had
been booked. `meetingUrl` is the organizer's Meet or Teams link, once their event made it. `cancelledByCandidate`
is true when the candidate cancelled it. `createdByUserId` is null when a workflow action offered it.
`newTimesOfferedAt` is set while the team's offer of new times for a booked interview waits for the candidate: the
booked time (`startsAt`) stays held, and `windowStart` and `windowEnd` are the new window. The end of that
window ends the offer.

ApplicationNoteDetail.description: A note as it stands: its latest text, its author and when it was written and last edited.

ApplicationRating.description:
The candidate's rating (ADR-0013 decision 13): one to five stars averaged from people's scorecards. Each rating answer
maps onto 1 to 5 (a 1 to 10 answer spread so that 1 counts as 1 and 10 as 5, a rating Yes as 5 and No as 1), each
scorecard counts once as the mean of its answered rating questions, and the rating is the mean of those, to one
decimal. It is people's judgement of the work only: never verification results, AI signals or the stage. No automation
reads it. A reviewer who still has their own scorecard to give reads `AfterYourScorecard`, with no value, until
they give it, so it cannot anchor them.

ApplicationSource.description: Where an application came from. Automation conditions read it as `application.source`.

ApplicationStage.description: A stage of the job's workflow, as an application sees it.

ApplicationSummary.description:
An application in a list. No accommodation flag here: lists reach every reviewer, so it shows only on the
application itself.

ApplicationTaskEntry.description:
Something a person should do about an application: a review, a to-do, a rejection to decide on, or a scorecard a
teammate asked for. A review and a requested scorecard are done when the scorecard is submitted; the others are
ticked off by hand.

ApplicationTimelineEntry.description: One entry of an application's timeline, oldest first. Members that do not apply to the type are null.

ApplicationVerification.description:
An application's verification: two separate assessments, each a categorical level with reason codes, the signals and
their evidence and counter-evidence, a plain-language summary and a suggested next step (ADR-0004). There is no score
or percentage anywhere in it, and nothing here decides anything: every action is a person's, and every action is in
`reviewLog`, the audit trail the dashboard shows in the candidate's Activity.

ApplyTemplateUpdateRequest.description:
Replaces a job's workflow with a published version of the template it came from (usually the newest, from
`GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}/workflow/template-diff`). It replaces the job's own edits too, which the diff lists.
`expectedWorkflowVersion` works as in UpdateJobWorkflowRequest.

AuthenticityAssessmentView.description: Is this a real, unique, present person who is who they say they are?

Automation.description:
Trigger, conditions, actions (workflow-engine.md §2). Stored and validated structurally here; the workflow engine
runs them. DefinitionValidator refuses an automation that would reject anyone because of a verification
signal (ADR-0004).

AutomationAction.description:
One action. Which optional members apply depends on ActionType AutomationAction.Type; DefinitionValidator checks
that each type has what it needs and nothing else.

AutomationCondition.description:
One test of an application fact, such as `answers.work_authorization EqualTo no` (yes/no answers are
`yes` and `no`, choice answers are option ids). Facts are
`answers.{questionId}`, `verification.authenticity`, `verification.aiAssistance`,
`verification.result`, `application.tags`, `application.source`,
`application.hoursInStage` and, for a TriggerType.ReviewerDecision automation only,
`reviewer.recommendation`.

AutomationConditions.description:
Conditions combined with ConditionMatch AutomationConditions.Match; a rule with bool AutomationCondition.Negate is a "not". One
level on purpose: a recursive tree would make the JSON Schema and the generated client recursive too.

AutomationFacts.description:
What an automation's conditions can see about one application at the moment its trigger fired: the facts snapshot
(docs/architecture/workflow-engine.md §3). The engine stores it with every run, so a replay or an audit sees exactly
what the conditions saw. A fact that is null or empty here is absent: ConditionOperator.Exists is false
and every other test fails.

AutomationIssue.description:
An automation that did not do its job: blocked (a loop, the depth limit, a workflow that no longer validates) or
failed (an action failed after its retries). Newest first; the run has the full record.

AutomationRunEntry.description:
The audit record of one automation evaluated for one application (workflow-engine.md §2, guardrail 3): the trigger,
the facts its conditions saw, which rules held, and what each action did.

BillingOverview.description:
An organization's billing for its Owner (docs/architecture/billing.md). `available` is false when this ScreenHire
has no payment provider, and then nothing else is set and nothing is limited. `state` is where the organization
stands: on its free trial, paying, paying late, or ended (everything stays readable and open jobs stay open; only
publishing a new job stops). `trialEndsAt` is set during the trial. `nextPaymentAt` and
`nextPaymentAmount` are set while a subscription renews, and `cancelsAtPeriodEnd` says it will not.
`openJobs` counts the jobs open now and `activeJobLimit` is the plan's limit, null when it has none.
`canManage`: the provider has a customer, so the payment portal can open. `sandbox`: the local fake, not Stripe.
`taxAtCheckout`: Checkout calculates tax on top of the prices, so the page says "plus tax where it applies".

BillingPlan.description:
A plan. `monthlyPrice` is null until the owner sets it. `activeJobs` is the most jobs open at once, null with
no limit set; `unlimited` says there is none by design. `canSubscribe`: Checkout can start it here.

BillingPlanChangePreview.description:
What switching the live subscription to `plan` costs, in `currency`. `amountDueNow` is the prorated difference
charged when the owner confirms (0 when the new plan costs less: the credit stays on the account), then
`nextPaymentAmount` a month on `nextPaymentAt`. `prorationDate` is the instant both were priced at; send it back
with the confirmation so the charge is the one shown.

BillingRedirect.description: Where to send the browser next: the payment provider's page, or the sandbox's.

BoardSummary.description: A board an organization may post to, and what it can promise (docs/architecture/job-distribution.md §1).

BrandImageKind.description: What a brand image is for, which decides its limits (BrandImageRules).

BrandImageUploadRequest.description: Asks for a link to upload one brand image of `kind`: a PNG or JPEG of `sizeBytes`.

BrandingContrast.description:
The contrast check of the colours asked about, each null when it was not asked: whether every pair the colour is
used in reaches WCAG 2.2 AA, the text colour that goes on it, the pairs, and the nearest passing shade when it fails.

BrandingImage.description:
An uploaded brand image. `scanStatus` is the malware scan's: a Pending or Infected image cannot be saved or
served. `url` is its public address on the careers board, null until it may be served. `fileName` is the
name it was uploaded with.

CalendarAccount.description:
The member's connected calendar. `accountEmail` is the calendar owner's address when the provider says it.
`problem` is `NeedsReconnect` once the provider stopped accepting the connection.

CalendarAuthorization.description: Where to send the browser next: the provider's consent page (or the sandbox's).

CalendarProvider.description: Whose calendar a member connected. CalendarProvider.Sandbox is the local stand-in (Development and tests only).

CalendarProviderOption.description: A calendar the member can connect: its id, and the name the sheet shows.

CalendarStatus.description:
The signed-in member's calendar (docs/architecture/interview-scheduling.md). `providers` are the calendars they
can connect here, empty when this ScreenHire has none configured. `connection` is their own, null until they
connect one. No token is ever in an answer.

CandidateDetail.description: A candidate and every application they made to the organization.

CandidateEmailEntry.description:
One email to the candidate, for Messages: what went, when, and who or which automation sent it. `kept` is false
for an email sent before ScreenHire kept each email's copy: only its subject is known.

CandidateEmailIssue.description: Why ScreenHire no longer emails a candidate's address (reported by the email provider).

CandidateHistoryEntry.description:
One entry of a candidate's history across all of their applications: an entry of one application's timeline, with the
application and job it belongs to, newest first. It leaves out verification output (the Verification tab holds that,
ADR-0004) and what a reviewer scored or recommended (a scorecard entry says one was submitted, nothing more).

CandidateInput.description: The candidate of an application a person or an API key adds.

CandidateSearchHit.description: A candidate whose name or email matched, on one of their applications: the record to open.

CandidateSummary.description: A candidate: one person per email address within the organization.

ChangeBillingPlanRequest.description: Confirms the switch to `plan` priced at `prorationDate`, as the preview returned it.

ChangeMemberJobAccessRequest.description: Sets which jobs a member sees: all of them, or only the jobs whose hiring team they are on.

ChangeMemberRoleRequest.description: Gives a member another role: a built-in one, or Custom with the custom role's id.

ChangeValueKind.description: How the screen shows a detail's values.

CheckGroup.description:
The groups of checks an organization may turn off (verification-engine.md §10). Every analyzer belongs to exactly one
group (CheckGroup? CheckGroups.Of(string analyzerName)), so a new analyzer cannot escape a switch.

CheckGroupState.description: The one word a group of checks has on the Verification tab.

CheckGroupView.description:
What one group of checks did for an application. `found` counts its signals that count toward the level; `notes`
the others (AI help and context that never counts), which are information only. `state` is the one word for the group:
`Found` when `found` is above 0, else `InformationOnly` when `notes` is, else `NotChecked` (the
application was added by hand, so there was no careers form for this group to read), `TurnedOff` (the organization's
settings) or `NothingFound`. `checked` names what the group looks at. `note` is what the organization's
settings changed in it (it is turned off, or a trusted domain or network stopped a signal), when they did.

CheckNotRun.description:
A group of checks that did not run, or did not count something, because of the organization's settings: its group was turned
off, or a domain or network it trusts stopped a signal. `note` says which. A result without signals from this group is
not a clean result, and a reviewer reads this before relying on it.

CheckNotRunKind.description: Why an analyzer's run says it did not look, or did not count something, because of the organization's settings.

ColorContrast.description: One colour's check. `problems` says each failing pair in words, as a refused save does.

ComparedText.description: One side of a text comparison.

ConsistencyCheckView.description:
The LLM consistency check for an application: its status, why it did not run (`note`), and the prompt version and
models it ran with. Contradictions appear as `CNT_INCONSISTENCY` signals, each citing both spans.

ContrastPairCheck.description: One pair: `ratio` is cut down to one decimal, so a failing pair never reads as its minimum.

ContrastPairName.description: The pairs of colours the branding check measures (docs/design/design-system.md section 18).

CounterEvidence.description: Something that argues against a signal, in plain language, with optional evidence of its own.

CreateApiKeyRequest.description:
Creates a key. `scopes` is `["Read"]` or `["Read", "Write"]`, with `"VerificationRead"` added to
let the key read verification results. Only an owner can add `VerificationRead`; every read through such a key is
recorded in the verification review log (ADR-0021). `permitsPerMinute` lowers the key's rate limit below the
deployment's; null uses the deployment's.

CreateApplicationRequest.description:
A recruiter adds an application by hand, for a candidate who applied another way. The candidate is matched by email
within the organization and created if new. The public apply flow is the careers site's.

CreateApplicationTaskRequest.description: A task for the hiring team about one application, from a person or an API key.

CreatedApiKey.description:
A new key. `token` is shown this once and cannot be read again: send it as `Authorization: Bearer
{token}`.

CreateEmailTemplateRequest.description: A new template of the organization's own: its name, a Liquid subject and a Liquid plain-text body.

CreateHiringTemplateRequest.description:
A new organization template, whose version 1 is a draft. Give a `definition`, or `copyFromVersionId` to
start from an existing version (a system template's, to customise it), or neither for a basic pipeline.

CreateHiringTemplateVersionRequest.description: Starts the next version as a draft: the given definition, or a copy of the newest version's.

CreateJobRequest.description:
A new job. With `templateVersionId` (a published version of an own or system template), the job copies that
version's workflow, and every field left out here takes the template's posting default. Without a slug, one is made
from the title. The description is rich text as HTML, kept to the dashboard editor's elements (p, br, strong, em, h2,
h3, ul, ol, li and links to http, https or mailto addresses); anything else is removed with its text kept. Plain text
works too: a blank line starts a paragraph and lines starting with "- " make a list. The summary is the plain-text
line a careers card shows under the title, at most 160 characters; leave it out and the card uses the description's
first sentence.

CreateRoleRequest.description:
Makes a custom role by copying a role: a built-in one (`copyFrom`) or a custom one (`copyFromRoleId`), never
both. Owner-only permissions are never copied.

CreateScorecardTemplateRequest.description: A new scorecard of the organization's own, optionally a copy of another (`copiedFrom`, by id).

CreateViewRequest.description: Saves the current filters and sort as a view; a job view names its job, a candidates view takes none.

CreateWebhookEndpointRequest.description: A new webhook endpoint: where to post, and which events (`GET /v1/webhooks/event-types` lists them).

CurrentOrganization.description:
The organization the signed-in user works in, their role there (a built-in one, or Custom with `customRoleId`),
its name, and every permission it gives them, in catalogue order. The dashboard shows and hides controls by these;
the API checks the same permissions on every request (ADR-0014). `seesAllJobs` is false for a member on Only
jobs they're on, who sees just the jobs whose hiring team they are on (ADR-0015).

CurrentUser.description: The signed-in user, and the organization they work in (null until onboarding).

CustomizedText.description: One text of a board: its own (null when it follows the job) and the job's newest published one.

CustomizePostingRequest.description:
What one board receives in place of the job's title and description. A null or blank field follows the job, and so
does one equal to the job's own text; sending both null removes the customization. `jobVersion` is the version
the text was edited against (int PostingCustomization.JobVersion): a save against an older one is a 409.

CustomRoleDetail.description: One of the organization's custom roles, for its page. `copiedFrom` is the name of the role it started as.

DataRequestCandidate.description:
Who asked, while they are still in the organization's records: `id`, `name` and `email`. A request from
someone since erased has no candidate (`null`), and nothing about them is kept.

DataRequestEntry.description:
One candidate's request for a copy of their data or for it to be erased. `dueAt` is the team's target for an answer
and `overdue` says it has passed while the request is still open; neither is a promise to the candidate.
`copySentAt` is when the download link for a copy went out. `declineReason` is what the team told the candidate;
it is cleared if the candidate is erased.

DataRequestList.description:
The organization's data requests, earliest due date first: every open one, and those answered in the last 90 days.
`openCount` is how many are open.

DeclineDataRequestRequest.description: Declines a request. `reason` (1 to 500 characters) is emailed to the candidate, so it is written for them.

DeviceCheckBasis.description:
On which footing the careers page may compute a device fingerprint (docs/research/legal.md, "Device / browser
fingerprint"; verification-engine.md §3). ePrivacy Art. 5(3) needs consent for fingerprinting unless it is strictly
necessary, and data protection authorities differ on whether fraud prevention is, so the basis is configuration per
country rather than code. An organization may also choose one, but only to be more protective than its region
(DeviceCheckBasis DeviceCheckBases.MoreProtective(DeviceCheckBasis a, DeviceCheckBasis b)).

DismissReason.description: Why a reviewer dismissed an assessment.

DismissVerificationAssessmentRequest.description: Sets an assessment aside. A reason is required; `Other` also needs a note.

EditApplicationNoteRequest.description: The note's new text. Only its author edits a note; a mention the new text adds notifies only the person added.

EditSavedNoteRequest.description: Replaces a saved candidate's note. Blank clears it. The Activity entry from when they were saved keeps the first note.

EmailDirection.description: Which way an email in Messages went.

EmailPreview.description: An email as the candidate would receive it: the subject, the HTML part and the plain-text part.

EmailsQueued.description:
How many emails were queued. `skipped` counts applications the email does not fit: the stage-change email to a
candidate whose application has ended, and a candidate whose address bounced or marked an email as spam. Each sent email appears in its application's activity.

EmailTemplateDraft.description:
Wording to render with the sample candidate, before it is saved. `templateId` is the template it is for, so
the rejection email's `reason` renders; leave it out for a new template.

EmailTemplateEntry.description:
One email template. Built-in templates have ScreenHire's ids and names; the organization may change their wording
(`edited`) and restore it. Its own templates have a Guid id and its own name.

EmailTemplateList.description:
The organization's email templates and the variables they may use. `sendingEnabled` is false when this
deployment has no email sender: templates can still be edited, but nothing can be sent or tested.

EmailTemplateVariableEntry.description:
A variable a template may use as `{{ name }}`. `rejectOnly`: only the rejection email has it.
`questionnaireOnly`: only the follow-up questions email has it. `invitationOnly`: only the saved candidates
invitation or an interview email has it.

EraseCandidateRequest.description:
Erases a candidate. `confirmation` is the candidate's full name as the person typed it, compared ignoring case and
surrounding spaces, so an erasure is never one stray click.

EraseDataRequestRequest.description:
Erases the candidate behind an erasure request. `confirmation` is the candidate's full name as the person typed it,
compared ignoring case and surrounding spaces.

EvidenceKind.description: How a piece of evidence renders, so the dashboard can show any signal without code of its own per signal.

ExplainReason.description: Why a reviewer marked a reason explained.

ExplainVerificationReasonRequest.description: Marks one reason explained. A reason is required; `Other` also needs a note.

FieldTelemetryInput.description: Counts for one form field. `fieldId` is a question id or one of the form's own fields (`firstName`, ...).

FollowUpQuestionnaire.description:
A questionnaire the hiring team sends after the candidate applied, with a ActionType.SendQuestionnaire
action: the candidate answers it on the careers site through a signed link. Completing it fires
TriggerType.QuestionnaireCompleted automations that name it. File questions are not offered: the page
works without JavaScript and takes no uploads.

FunnelEnd.description: How an application ended, in the words a candidate sees. The employer's own stage names never reach the page.

FunnelStage.description: One row of the funnel: a stage kind and the applications that reached it or a later one.

HiringReport.description:
The Reports page (docs/architecture/reports.md): headline numbers, applications and hires by week, the funnel, time to
hire, sources and open jobs for the jobs the person can see, between two instants. All of it comes from one snapshot,
so the numbers agree. Nothing here reads verification (verification) results.

HiringTeamMember.description:
A person on a job's hiring team, or on a hiring template's default one (ADR-0015). `memberId` is their
membership's id, which the team stores. `seesAllJobs` says whether they see every job anyway; a member on Only
jobs they're on sees this job through this list.

HiringTeamRequest.description:
Sets a hiring team to `memberIds`, the organization's member ids. For a job, `copyFromJobId` also brings
over another job's team, which the caller must be able to see.

HiringTemplateDefinition.description: A hiring template version's full definition: the workflow a job copies, plus defaults for the job's posting.

HiringTemplateDetail.description: A hiring template with its versions, oldest first. `lastUpdated` counts every version's changes.

HiringTemplateSummary.description:
A hiring template in a list. System templates ship with the product and are read-only. An archived template
(`archived`) is out of the pickers: no new job starts from it, and the jobs that did keep their copy.

HiringTemplateVersionDetail.description:
One version of a hiring template with its full definition. The definition's JSON Schema is served at
`/v1/schemas/hiring-template-definition.json`. A draft saves with problems: `problems` lists what stops it
from being tested or published, in the validator's words (an empty list when it is ready), so a client need not call
the validate route after a save.

HiringWorkflow.description:
What a hiring template versions and a job copies: the stage pipeline, the screening questionnaire, the
automations and the follow-up questionnaires a ActionType.SendQuestionnaire action sends.

HistoryDetail.description:
A value before and after. Equal values did not change and show for context; a null `before` is new and a null
`after` was removed. An `Instant` is ISO 8601, for the browser to format.

HistoryEntry.description: Everything one save changed in the object: who, when, and a line per change.

HistoryLine.description:
One change in words, such as "made Notes on the exercise optional". `text` is the sentence; `parts` are its
runs, with the name of the thing that changed marked `strong`. `details` are its values before and after.

HistoryPage.description:
One page of an object's history, newest first. `nextBefore` is the id of this page's last entry, to pass as
`before` for the next page, or null after the last.

Interviewer.description:
A member who can interview for a job: one who sees it (everyone who sees all jobs, and the members on its hiring team).
`calendarConnected` is true when their calendar is connected and works here, so ScreenHire can read when they are
busy and put the interview in it; an interview cannot be offered with someone who has none. `calendarProvider`
says which calendar it is, and is null when `calendarConnected` is false.

InterviewParticipant.description:
One interviewer on an interview and the state of their calendar event. `syncStatus` is `Pending` (not on the
calendar yet, or being changed), `Synced` or `Failed`; `syncProblem` says why in plain words when it
failed. `displayName` is "Former member" for someone who left the organization.

InterviewSyncStatus.description: Where one interviewer's calendar event stands.

InvitationAcceptance.description: Accepts the invitation whose token an emailed link carries, signing in as the invited address.

InvitationDetails.description: What an open invitation offers: the organization's name and the role's, such as "Recruiter" or a custom role as typed.

InvitationLookup.description: Asks which organization and role the invitation whose token an emailed link carries offers. It uses nothing up.

InvitationPreviewRequest.description: The invitation as `candidateId` would receive it, for `jobId`.

InvitationRequest.description:
Invites a person by email to join the organization with a role: a built-in one, or Custom with its id. They join with
`jobAccess`, All when it is left out.

InvitationsQueued.description:
How many invitations were queued, and how many candidates were skipped: no longer in the pool, or already applied to
the job. Each sent invitation appears in Messages and in the Activity of the application they were kept from.

InviteToApplyRequest.description: Invites these saved candidates to apply for `jobId`, an open job.

JobAccess.description:
Which jobs a member sees (ADR-0015): every job, or only the jobs whose hiring team they are on
(List<Guid> Job.HiringTeam). Stored as text on the membership and on an invitation.

JobAiUse.description:
The AI-use policy the apply form asks under for one job. The organization sets `organizationDefault` once
(Verification) and a job may override it with `override`; `policy` is the one in force, the override when
there is one. The question itself is asked on every application, and no automation reads the answer.

JobBoardInfo.description: A tenant's board in the public job-board API (Greenhouse-style: `GET /v1/public/boards/{organizationSlug}`).

JobBoardJob.description:
A job in the public job-board API, in Greenhouse's snake_case shape so tools built for Greenhouse boards read it.
`content` is the description as sanitized HTML (Greenhouse escapes it; we do not), present with
`?content=true` and on a single job. Ids are our job ids (UUIDs), not Greenhouse's integers.

JobBoardJobList.description: Every job on a tenant's public job board (Greenhouse-style `jobs` and `meta.total`).

JobBoardPayRange.description: Greenhouse's pay transparency range, in minor units of `currency_type`.

JobDetail.description: Everything about one job: posting content, lifecycle, its workflow copy and where that came from.

JobLocation.description:
A place the job is based: schema.org `PostalAddress` without the street. string? JobLocation.Country is an ISO 3166-1
alpha-2 code. The API requires it; a location carried over from the old free-text column may lack it.

JobPostingStatus.description: One job on one board: where it stands and what is still uncertain.

JobSalary.description: A pay range. At least one of decimal? JobSalary.Min and decimal? JobSalary.Max is set; string JobSalary.Currency is ISO 4217.

JobSnapshot.description:
The posting content of a job at one moment: everything a careers page, a feed or a job board shows. A
JobVersion freezes one. Equality compares the content, list members included. `summary` is
the written summary only (null while the card follows the description); a version frozen before the field existed has none.

JobSummary.description: A job as shown in the recruiter dashboard's list.

JobTemplateDiff.description:
How the job's workflow differs from the newest published version of the template it came from. Empty
`changes` with `updateAvailable` false: the job is up to date.

JobTemplateSource.description: The template version a job's workflow was copied from, and whether a newer one is published.

JobTimeToHire.description: One job's hires in the range and their median days from applying to being hired.

JobVersionDetail.description: One published version of a job: the frozen content boards were sent.

JobVersionSummary.description: One published version of a job, without its content.

KeepInMindRequest.description:
Saves the candidates of these applications: each leaves its job without a rejection and joins the saved candidates.
`note` says why, once for all of them. Only an open application whose candidate gave permission for future roles
on its form can be saved.

KeptInMind.description:
What happened: `kept` were saved; `notAllowed` have no permission for future roles (they never gave it or
they took it back); `alreadyEnded` were hired, rejected, withdrawn or saved already.

Knockout.description:
Marks a yes/no question as an objective eligibility check (work authorisation, a required licence). The answer
bool Knockout.DisqualifyingAnswer makes the candidate ineligible. It never rejects anyone by itself: an automation
decides, and by default it only queues the application for a person to review (workflow-engine.md §2).

LastUpdate.description: When a tracked object last changed and who changed it, the last fact in its header.

LlmProvenance.description:
Which prompt and models produced an LLM-derived signal, for audit (verification-engine.md §5). The model ids are the
ones the provider reported serving, not the configured names.

LlmSource.description: Whose model answers the consistency check.

MagicLinkRequest.description:
Asks for a sign-in link by email. `returnUrl` is a path on the dashboard to open after the link is used, such as an
assistant's request to connect; anything that is not a local path is dropped.

MagicLinkVerification.description: Redeems the token from an emailed sign-in link.

ManualAutomationQueued.description: A manual automation was queued. `eventId` keys its run: find it in the application's automation runs.

MemberJob.description: A job whose hiring team a member is on, for their access sheet. Changed through the job's own hiring team.

MemberNotificationSettings.description:
The signed-in member's settings for teammates' changes as toasts, in their current organization. `toasts` turns
them on or off; `closeToasts` closes each after a few seconds, and off keeps it until dismissed; `off` lists
the kinds of change that do not toast. Everything starts on.

MembershipLogEntry.description:
One entry in the organization's membership log. `actorUserId` made the change, or `actorApiKeyId` when an
API key did; `memberUserId` is who it is
about (null for an invitation not accepted yet and for a change to a role itself). `previousRole` and
`role` are set where the kind has them, with the custom role's id and its name at the time; for RoleCreated,
RoleUpdated and RoleDeleted, `customRoleId` and `roleName` are the role, and a rename keeps the old name in
`previousRoleName`. JobAccessChanged sets `previousJobAccess` and `jobAccess`; an invitation and a
join set `jobAccess`. AddedToHiringTeam and RemovedFromHiringTeam name a job (`jobId`, with its title now)
or a hiring template's default team (`hiringTemplateId`, with its name now). A reader who sees only their own
jobs gets no entries about the others. The data request kinds and CandidateErased from a request set `dataRequestId`
(an id only, never the candidate); RetentionApplied sets `itemCount`, the applications it deleted.

ModelPresetView.description:
A provider preset: `baseUrl` is the address it fills in (null when the person enters one, or for Anthropic),
`baseUrlEditable` says the person enters it (Azure OpenAI's resource, any other endpoint), and `listsModels`
says the provider's models endpoint lists what a key can use.

MoveApplicationRequest.description:
Moves an application to another stage of its job's workflow. Only people move applications here. The optional
`note` is kept on the move's timeline entry.

MyOrganization.description:
One of the signed-in user's organizations, for the organization switcher, with their role there. `roleName` is
null for a custom role in an organization other than the one they work in: row-level security keeps its roles from
them until they switch.

NotificationItem.description:
One notification in the signed-in member's bell. The dashboard builds the plain line from `kind` and `payload`,
so the wording lives in one place and a kind it does not know still shows with its link.

NotificationList.description: The member's notifications that are not dismissed, newest first, and how many of all of them are unread.

OAuthAuthorizationRequestInfo.description:
An assistant's request to connect, as the consent page shows it: who is asking, where the person goes afterwards, which
organization the connection would belong to, and what it may do. `redirectHost` is the address's host (and port, for
a local one); `redirectIsLoopback` is true for an address on this person's own computer.

OAuthAuthorizeRequest.description:
The person's decision on an assistant's request: the OAuth parameters the assistant sent, copied as they came, plus
`approve` and the scopes the person chose. `grantedScopes` is cut to what the assistant asked for and the person
holds, and always includes Read.

OAuthAuthorizeResult.description: Where to send the person next: the assistant's redirect address, carrying the code or the refusal.

OAuthConnectionSummary.description:
An assistant a person connected to this organization. It acts with `scopes` and shows in activity under its name.
`lastUsedAt` is accurate to about a minute; `revokedAt` is set once a connection is revoked, and the row stays.

OAuthScopeOffer.description:
One thing the assistant asked to be allowed. `grantable` is false when the signed-in person does not hold it
themselves; `reason` says why. Read is always offered and always granted.

OfferNewInterviewTimesRequest.description:
Offers the candidate new times for a booked interview: they pick from `windowStart` to `windowEnd` (at most 90
days), in the interview's own length, working hours and zone. The booked time stays held until they pick, and the
events in every calendar then move. Offering again replaces the window.

OnboardingRequest.description: Creates the signed-in user's organization, with them as its Owner.

OrganizationBranding.description:
The organization's branding (docs/architecture/branding.md): the brand colour (buttons and links), the second colour
(the header band of its careers pages and emails), the heading font and the images in use, each null for
ScreenHire's default. `lastUpdated` is the branding's last change ("by ScreenHire" while it is all the
default); its history is `/branding/history`.

OrganizationProfile.description:
The signed-in user's organization. `slug` names its careers pages and public API routes and does not change after
onboarding; `careersUrl` is its careers board on the configured careers domain, where `{careersUrl}/embed.js`
is the embeddable widget's script. `questionsPerPage` is how many questions candidates see on each page of a
questionnaire that has no sections. `embedOrigins` are the sites allowed to show the careers pages in a frame
(origins such as `https://www.example.com`, in the order they were added). `lastUpdated` is the last change
to the name, the questions per page or the sites, or when the organization was made; its history is
`/v1/organization/history`.

OrganizationRetention.description:
The organization's record retention. `months` is how long after it ended an application stays before it is deleted
(1 to 120), or `null` for never, the default. `lastUpdated` is the last change ("by ScreenHire" while it is
the default); its history is `/v1/organization/data-retention/history`. `lastRun` is the newest run that deleted
something, or `null` when none has.

OrganizationRole.description:
The four roles ScreenHire supplies, most access first, and OrganizationRole.Custom for a role the organization made
(CustomRole). Stored as text.

OrganizationSendingDomain.description:
The organization's sending domain (Settings, Sending domain). `available` is false when this deployment has no email
provider: the page says so and offers nothing. `sandbox` says the records are made up for a local run. `domain`
is null until one is added. `lastUpdated` is the newest change to it (added, verified, no longer verified), null with
no domain; its History is `GET /v1/organization/sending-domain/history`.

OrganizationVerificationSettings.description:
The organization's verification settings (verification-engine.md §10). `llmConsistencyCheck` turns on the LLM
consistency check, which sends the resume, answers and any LinkedIn export to the model provider; it is off until an admin
turns it on. `limits` is the monthly AI budget and cap with what has been used so far this month; it is null for a
member who cannot see AI usage (`ViewAiUsage`), and an Owner changes it with `/v1/organization/ai-usage/limits`.
`presets` are the providers an organization can bring a key for, with the address each fills in.
`ownKeyInputPrice` and `ownKeyOutputPrice` are what the organization's own key costs it, in US dollars per million
tokens (null when unknown, or for a member who cannot edit settings).

PageTelemetryInput.description:
Page-level counts: times the page was hidden, and automation markers from a fixed list (`webdriver`,
`headless`, ...).

PageTimeInput.description: The active seconds on one page of the apply form (`details`, `page-2`, `review`).

PasskeyList.description: The signed-in person's passkeys, newest first, and how many they may keep.

PasskeyOptions.description:
The WebAuthn options the browser passes to `navigator.credentials.create` or `get`, as the JSON text the
W3C `PublicKeyCredential*OptionsJSON` shape defines. The browser parses it with
`PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON` or `parseRequestOptionsFromJSON`.

PasskeySignInRequest.description: The browser's answer to a sign-in ceremony: `credential.toJSON()` as text.

PasskeySummary.description: One of the signed-in person's passkeys. `id` is the credential id, base64url.

PendingInvitation.description: An invitation nobody has accepted, revoked or let expire yet, and the role and job access it offers.

Permission.description:
Something a role lets a person do. The ids are stable: custom roles store them. Names and descriptions are in
RolePermissions.

PermissionGroup.description: The groups the Roles page shows permissions in.

PermissionSummary.description:
A permission in the order the Roles page lists it: its group, its name and one line on what it covers.
`ownerOnly` ones never go into a custom role; `everyRole` ones are in every role.

PostingCustomization.description:
A board's customization, for the Customize sheet: each text with the job's, and what the job changed since the
board's own was written against it. `jobVersion` is the published version the job's text comes from.

PostingDefaults.description: Values a new job starts with when it is created from the template. Every member is optional.

PostingPreview.description: What a board would receive for a draft customization, and what its checks say about it. Nothing is saved.

PostingTextChange.description: A text of the job that changed since the board's own was written. Both are plain text.

PreviewBillingPlanChangeRequest.description: The plan to price a switch to, by its key from the plan list.

PublicApplicationDraft.description:
A saved draft as the careers apply page fills the form from it. `jobSlug` is the job it belongs to; the page
refuses a draft for another job.

PublicApplicationDraftReceipt.description: A saved draft: the token in its link, which the careers page keeps to save it again, and when it is deleted.

PublicApplicationDraftRequest.description:
What a candidate saves of the apply form to finish later (ApplicationDraft): their details, their
answers to the non-file questions, the assistive-technology switch and the AI-use answer. Nothing is required yet
beyond the first name and the email the link goes to.

PublicApplicationForm.description:
Everything the careers apply page needs for one open job. The resume question comes first
(ApplicationForm). `turnstileSiteKey` is null unless the bot challenge is configured.
`telemetry` is a new telemetry session for the form; the page keeps the first one it gets.
`sections` are the questionnaire's named pages, or null to split it into pages of `questionsPerPage`
(apply-flow.md §7). `saveDraftEnabled` says whether the candidate can save the form to finish later: false when
this deployment sends no email or has no careers host to link to.

PublicApplicationRequest.description:
A candidate's application from the careers page. The candidate is matched by email within the organization and
created if new; an existing candidate's details are never changed by a public submission.

PublicBrandImage.description: A brand image as a public page links it: `url` is the same for every page, email and person.

PublicCandidateInput.description: The candidate as the apply form asks: a first name, an optional last name, the email and an optional phone.

PublicDataDownload.description: A short-lived address that downloads the candidate's copy.

PublicDataRequestChoice.description: The candidate's choice: a copy of their data, or its erasure.

PublicDataRequestForm.description:
What the careers data request page needs before it asks for an address. `enabled` is false where the deployment
sends no email or has no careers host to link to: the page then keeps its "write to the employer" text.
`turnstileSiteKey` is null unless the bot challenge is configured.

PublicDataRequestLinkRequest.description:
The address a candidate types to be sent the link that opens their choices. The answer to it is the same whether or not
the address has applied, so it tells nobody who has.

PublicDataRequestLinkStatus.description: What a valid emailed link opens: the organization the candidate will be asking, by name.

PublicDataRequestReceipt.description:
The request the choice created, or the one that was already open. It never carries the team's due date, which is a
target on their dashboard and not a promise to the candidate.

PublicHeaderColors.description: The header band: its fill, the second colour, and the white or ink text on it. Both `#rrggbb`.

PublicInterview.description:
The interview as the candidate's page shows it. `slots` are the start times offered, as UTC instants in order, each
`durationMinutes` long: for an Open interview, and for a Booked one the candidate may still change. The page writes
them in `timeZone` (the `tz` asked for when it is a zone the server knows, otherwise `defaultTimeZone`,
the zone the team chose). `slotsUnavailable` is true when the team's calendars could not be read just now, so no
times are offered; trying again later may work. `minNoticeHours` is how long before the start the candidate can
still move or cancel. `newTimesOffered` is true while the team's offer of new times waits for the candidate: the
booked time stays until they pick, and they may move or cancel it whatever the notice, until the offered days end.
Nothing about the interviewers, and nothing from verification.

PublicInterviewChoice.description: The start time the candidate picked, one of the offered `slots`.

PublicInterviewState.description: Where a candidate's interview stands on the careers page.

PublicJob.description: A job as shown on a public careers page.

PublicJobBoard.description:
The public careers listing for one organization. `url` is the board's careers page; `branding` is its
branding, each part null for ScreenHire's; `embedOrigins` are the sites allowed to show it in a frame.

PublicOrganization.description:
An organization as its careers pages show it, with its branding (each part null for ScreenHire's) and
`embedOrigins`, the sites allowed to show the careers pages in a frame, which the pages send in their
`frame-ancestors` header (empty: none but the careers pages themselves).

PublicPalette.description:
The careers-page colours from the brand colour (docs/design/design-system.md section 18): `brand` fills,
`onBrand` is text on it, `brandText` is links on the page and `brandUi` is borders and focus rings.
A colour saved since the contrast check passes as it is, so all three are the colour itself; an older one is darkened
until it passes. All `#rrggbb`.

PublicPortal.description: Everything a candidate's page shows on its first screen.

PublicPortalApplication.description: One of the candidate's applications to this organization.

PublicPortalAttachment.description: A file sent with a reply, as base64 text.

PublicPortalDraft.description: An application the candidate started and saved to finish later; `token` opens the job's apply page with it.

PublicPortalForm.description:
What the careers portal page needs before it asks for an address. `enabled` is false where the deployment sends no
email or has no careers host to link to: the page then says the portal is not available here.
`turnstileSiteKey` is null unless the bot challenge is configured.

PublicPortalFunnel.description:
Where an application stands on the four fixed steps every job shares. `current` is an index into `steps`, or
null once the application ended, and then `ended` says how. Nothing about the employer's own stages is in it.

PublicPortalLinkRequest.description:
The address a candidate types to be sent the link to their page. The answer to it is the same whether or not the
address has applied, so it tells nobody who has.

PublicPortalMessage.description: One message in an application's thread: the email as the candidate got it, or their reply. Plain text only.

PublicPortalMessageDirection.description: Who wrote a message on the page: the team (an email ScreenHire sent for them) or the candidate.

PublicPortalMessages.description: An application's thread, oldest first. `canReply` is false until the team has written once.

PublicPortalReplyRequest.description:
A reply written on the page. `key` is the form's own random id (32 hex digits), so sending the same form twice stores one
reply.

PublicPortalWaiting.description:
Something the candidate can act on, with the token of the existing careers page for it
(`/questionnaires/{token}` or `/interviews/{token}`). The name of a questionnaire is the team's wording for it
and is not sent.

PublicPortalWaitingKind.description: What something is waiting on the candidate for.

PublicQuestion.description:
One question of a job's application form, as a candidate sees it. Knockout settings stay on the server: the form
accepts every answer, and a person reviews what follows from it.

PublicQuestionnaire.description:
A follow-up questionnaire as its careers page shows it, through the signed link in the candidate's email.
`questions`, `sections` and `draft` are listed only while the link is `Open`; knockout settings stay
on the server. `sections` are its named pages, or null to split it into pages of `questionsPerPage`.
`draft` holds the answers the candidate saved to finish later, empty when there are none.

PublicQuestionnaireAnswers.description: The candidate's answers to a follow-up questionnaire, keyed by question id as on the apply form.

PublicQuestionnaireStatus.description:
Whether a follow-up questionnaire's link can still be answered: `Answered` once the candidate sent their answers,
`Expired` after the link's time ran out, `Closed` when the questionnaire, the job or the application is no
longer open.

PublicTalentPoolStatus.description:
The page a candidate opens from the link in an invitation to stop being kept. `kept`: the organization still
keeps their details for future roles; false once they stopped it.

PublicTelemetrySettings.description:
What the careers page's telemetry module may do on this form (verification-engine.md §3): `sessionToken` binds its
snapshots to one way through the form, and `deviceCheck` is the footing for the device fingerprint where the job
is (`Off`, `Notice`, or `Consent`, which needs the candidate's tick).

PublicUploadSettings.description: Limits on candidate uploads. `origin` is where upload links point, for the page's content security policy.

PublishJobRequest.description:
Publishing a job: optionally, the boards to post it to. Left out, the first publish posts to every board in
`GET /v1/boards` and a later one updates the boards the job is already on. Naming a board the job was taken
down from posts it again.

Question.description:
One screening question. Which optional members apply depends on QuestionType Question.Type: IReadOnlyList<QuestionOption>? Question.Options for the
choice types, Knockout? Question.Knockout for QuestionType.YesNo, decimal? Question.Min and decimal? Question.Max
for QuestionType.Number, int? Question.MaxLength for the text types and
IReadOnlyList<string>? Question.AcceptedFileTypes for QuestionType.File.

Questionnaire.description: The screening questions a candidate answers when applying.

QuestionSection.description: One named page of a questionnaire: its name, the page's heading, and the ids of its questions in order.

RatingState.description:
`NotRated`: no scorecard with a rating answer yet. `Rated`: see `value`. `AfterYourScorecard`: the
reader has a review to give first.

ReceivedAttachment.description:
A file that came with a reply. It can be downloaded once `scanStatus` is `Clean` or `NotScanned`; while it is
`Pending` the download answers 409, and an `Infected` file is never offered.

ReceivedEmail.description:
A candidate's reply as it arrived: who it is from, the subject, the sanitized HTML part (may be empty) and the plain-text
part, and the files that came with it. `autoReply` marks an out-of-office or other automatic answer.

RegisterPasskeyRequest.description: The browser's answer to a registration ceremony, and the name to give the passkey (a device, as the person typed it).

RemoveFromTalentPoolRequest.description:
Takes the candidate out of the saved candidates. `candidateAsked`: they asked to be removed, so their permission for
future roles is withdrawn too, and they cannot be saved again until they give it on a new application.

ReportHeadline.description: The headline numbers of one range.

ReportOpenJob.description: An open job: when it opened, applications in the range, applications in an Interview stage now, days open and hires in the range.

ReportWeek.description: One Monday-start week: applications submitted in it and hires made in it, both inside the range.

RequestScorecardRequest.description:
Ask a teammate for a scorecard: a Scorecard task assigned to them, done when they submit that scorecard for the
application.

RetentionLastRun.description: When a retention run last deleted applications, and how many (the latest batch, when a run took several).

RetentionPreview.description:
What saving a period would delete right now: `applications` that ended before it, belonging to `candidates`
different people. Saved candidates are never counted.

RoleCatalogue.description:
The organization's roles and what each can do: the four built-in ones, most access first, then its custom roles by
name, with every permission in the catalogue (RolePermissions).

RoleSummary.description:
A role: built-in (`customRoleId` null), or Custom with its id. `description` is one line on what it is
for, generated from its permissions for a custom role. `people` counts the members who have it. A built-in role
is last updated by ScreenHire.

RuleResult.description: One rule's result, so an audit or a simulation shows which conditions held.

SalaryRequest.description: A pay range. Currency and period may come from the template's posting defaults on create.

SandboxBoardListing.description: One listing on the local sandbox board, as the board itself would show it.

SavedViewSummary.description:
A saved view as the signed-in member sees it: their own, and the team's shared ones. `mine` is whether they saved
it; `canEdit` whether they may rename, share or delete it (its owner, or a role that edits anyone's views).

ScheduleInterviewRequest.description:
Offers an application's candidate an interview. `interviewerUserIds` are one to five members who see the job; the
first is the organizer, whose calendar event invites the candidate and makes the meeting link. `durationMinutes`
is 15, 30, 45, 60, 90 or 120. The candidate picks a start that fits inside `windowStart` and `windowEnd`
(at most 90 days) within the working hours `dayStart` and `dayEnd` (`HH:mm`, default 09:00 and 17:00,
weekdays only) in `timeZone` (an IANA id such as `Europe/London`), which is also the zone the candidate's page
first shows.

Scorecard.description:
A job's copy of a library scorecard: the questions a reviewer answers for a stage, then an overall
Recommendation and a note, which every scorecard has. Submitting one raises the
TriggerType.ReviewerDecision trigger with the recommendation as the `reviewer.recommendation` fact.
Rating questions average into the candidate's rating (ADR-0013, `RatingRule`); nothing else on a scorecard
does, and no automation reads the rating. Questions are about the job (skills, experience, the work itself), never
personality, emotion or honesty (CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 3); DefinitionValidator refuses questions that
name those.

ScorecardAnswerInput.description:
The answer to one question: `value` for the yes-or-no kinds ("yes" or "no"), a choice (an option id) and the
text kinds, `values` for a multi-choice (option ids) and `rating` for a number scale.

ScorecardEntry.description:
One reviewer's scorecard, given while the application was in a stage: an answer to each question as it was asked, and
an overall recommendation.
Its rating answers make the candidate's rating (`ApplicationRating`, ADR-0013); nothing else on it does.

ScorecardQuestion.description: One scorecard question. IReadOnlyList<QuestionOption>? ScorecardQuestion.Options apply to the choice types only.

ScorecardQuestionType.description:
A scorecard question's answer kind. The General kinds share QuestionType's names. The Rating kinds are
the ones the candidate's rating averages: ScorecardQuestionType.Rating5 (1 to 5), ScorecardQuestionType.Rating10 (1 to 10) and
ScorecardQuestionType.RatingYesNo (yes or no).

ScorecardRating.description: A v0.2 criterion as the reviewer was asked it, and their labelled rating; null when they did not rate it.

ScorecardTemplateDetail.description: One library scorecard with its questions. Every scorecard then asks for an overall recommendation and a note.

ScorecardTemplateSummary.description:
A scorecard in the organization's library: a built-in (`builtIn`, ScreenHire's and read only) or one of its own.
A hiring template's stage names it by `id` (`scorecardTemplateId`); a job keeps its own copy.

SearchResults.description:
What a search found among the candidates and jobs the reader sees: candidates by name or email, one hit per
application, and jobs by title. Each list is short and starts with names or titles that begin with the search.

SendEmailsRequest.description:
An email to the candidates of these applications, one each, rendered for each candidate. Give the wording
(`subject` and `body`, Liquid over the general variables), a `templateId` to send the template as it
stands, or both: then the wording goes, changed for this send only, and the template id records where it started.
A blank email has wording and no template id.

SendingDomainDetail.description:
A sending domain and what is left to do. `status` is Verified only once the email provider confirms the records,
and only then does mail come from `fromAddress`; until then it keeps ScreenHire's address.

SendingDomainRecordEntry.description: One DNS record to add at the domain's DNS host, why it is needed, and what the last check found.

SendingDomainRecordPurpose.description: Why a record is on the list.

SendingDomainRecordState.description: What the last DNS lookup found for a record.

SentEmail.description: An email exactly as it went to the candidate: the address, the subject, the HTML part and the plain-text part.

SetJobAiUseRequest.description:
Sets a job's own AI-use policy, or follows the organization's again when `policy` is null. It is a route of its own
rather than a field of UpdateJobRequest, which replaces the posting and would clear it when left out.

SetSendingDomainRequest.description: The domain to send from, such as `example.com`. Replaces the organization's current one.

SignalCategory.description:
Independent kinds of evidence. A level above the lowest needs two of them (verification-engine.md §2), so that one noisy
source, such as a corporate VPN, cannot raise a level by itself.

SignalConfidence.description: How sure the analyzer is of the observation itself (a lookup that matched exactly, or a heuristic).

SignalEvidence.description:
One piece of evidence. One flat record for every kind, members that do not apply left null, like timeline data, so
the JSON column, the API and the generated client stay one simple shape. EvidenceKind SignalEvidence.Kind says which members apply.
A metric is a measurement (seconds, a count), never a likelihood or a score.

SignalWeight.description: How much a signal counts towards its category. Categorical on purpose: there is no score (ADR-0004).

SignInMethods.description: How a person can sign in here: the configured identity providers, and whether email links work.

SignInProvider.description: An identity provider button on the sign-in page.

SimulatedAutomation.description: What one automation would do. Only automations the trigger fires are listed, in definition order.

SimulateWorkflowRequest.description:
"Test this workflow" (workflow-engine.md §4): run a sample application through a workflow and see which automations
a trigger would fire. Nothing is saved or sent. `facts` is the sample application's snapshot; leave members out
for facts it does not have.

SlackAccount.description:
The member's linked Slack account: its name, and whether mentions and tasks given to them arrive as direct
messages. `problem` is `CannotMessage` when Slack refused the last one.

SlackAuthorization.description: Where to send the browser next: Slack's page (or the sandbox's) for an OAuth round trip.

SlackChannelChoice.description: A channel by Slack's id and its name, without the `#`.

SlackChannelEvent.description: What the team can have posted to its channel. The names are stored; never rename one.

SlackChannelOption.description: A channel the app can post to. `isPrivate`: only for invited members, the app among them.

SlackSettings.description:
The workspace's settings: the channel (null until picked), the events posted there, who connected it and when,
and why posting stopped working, if it did.

SlackStatus.description:
Slack for the signed-in member (docs/architecture/slack.md). `available` is false when this ScreenHire has no
Slack app, and then nothing else is set. `workspace` is null until someone connects one. `account` is the
member's own link. `settings` is there only for someone who manages integrations and sees every job. The bot
token is never in any answer.

SlackTestResult.description: Whether the test message reached the channel, and if not, why.

SlackWorkspace.description: The connected workspace, as every member sees it. `disconnected`: Slack stopped taking the app's token.

SourceCount.description: Applications submitted in the range from one source, and how many of them are hired now.

StageDays.description: The median days the hires made in the range spent in one stage kind, and how many of them were in it.

StartBillingCheckoutRequest.description: The plan to subscribe to, by its key from the plan list.

StartCalendarConnectRequest.description: Connects the member's calendar. `returnUrl`: the dashboard path to come back to, a local path only.

StartSlackLinkRequest.description: Links the member's Slack account. `returnUrl`: the dashboard path to come back to, a local path only.

SubmitScorecardRequest.description:
A reviewer's scorecard. Name one of two: `stageId`, a stage the application has reached whose workflow stage
has a scorecard (the job's own copy), or `scorecardTemplateId`, a library scorecard given at the stage the
application is in now. Each reviewer gives one per stage and scorecard: the same submission again returns the stored
one, a different one is a 409.

SwitchOrganizationRequest.description: Makes another of the signed-in user's organizations the one they work in.

TalentPoolList.description:
The organization's saved candidates (docs/architecture/talent-pool.md): the candidates the team saved, whose permission
for future roles still holds. They stay until the team removes them or the candidate asks to stop.

TaskListItem.description: A task in a list across applications (My tasks): the task, and the candidate and job it is about.

TaskScope.description:
Whose tasks a list shows: the signed-in person's (assigned to them), the team's (assigned to nobody in particular),
or everyone's (every task the person can see).

TaskStatusFilter.description: Which tasks a list shows: the open ones, or the ones done.

TeamMember.description:
A member of the signed-in user's organization. `id` is the membership's id, which the member routes take.
`role` is a built-in role or Custom, with `customRoleId` naming which; `roleName` is its name either way.
`jobAccess` is their stored choice and `seesAllJobs` what applies: Owners and Admins see all jobs whatever
it says (ADR-0015). `jobCount` counts the jobs whose hiring team they are on, among the jobs the reader sees.
`lastUpdated` is the newest change to their membership (a role or job access change) and who made it; null when
nothing has changed since they joined, which `joinedAt` already says, and for a reader who cannot manage the team.

TelemetrySnapshotInput.description:
One cumulative snapshot of one page view's form telemetry: session aggregates only (CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 4), never
keystrokes, key values, timings per key or field content. Unknown members are refused, so nothing else can travel in
it.

TemplateUsageList.description: Every template's use, by kind, as the Templates page lists them.

TemplateUse.description:
Where one template is used and when it was last used. `templateId` is the id its own list gives it.
`usedBy` lists every user, so its length is the count: jobs that are not closed for a hiring template, hiring
templates for a scorecard, automations for an email. `lastUsedAt`: when a job last started from it, a stage last
used it or an email last went out from it; null when never. `notUsedRecently`: nothing used it in the last 180
days, and the team has had it longer than that.

TestEmailSent.description: A test send went to the signed-in person's own address.

TimeToHire.description: Days from applying to being hired, for the hires made in the range.

ToastKind.description:
A kind of teammate's change a member can turn off. The first six are about a candidate on a job whose hiring team
they are on; ToastKind.Tasks is a task assigned to them; ToastKind.Templates a hiring template they changed
last, published by someone else. Stored and sent as text.

UpdateAiUsageLimitsRequest.description:
Sets the monthly budget and cap. Both are in `unit` (whole tokens, or dollars to the cent); null removes one. With
`Money` and an own key, the own key's prices must be set, since a call with no known cost counts as nothing.

UpdateBrandingRequest.description:
Replaces the whole branding. Colours are `#rrggbb` and must pass the contrast check
(`/branding/contrast`); each image id is one of the organization's uploads of that kind that passed its scan.
Null is ScreenHire's default, or no image.

UpdateCareersEmbeddingRequest.description:
Replaces the sites allowed to embed the careers pages, at most 20. Each is an https site's address; a bare name gets
https and a page's address keeps only its site, so `www.example.com/careers` saves as
`https://www.example.com`. Duplicates are dropped and the order is kept. An empty list lets no other site frame
the careers pages.

UpdateEmailTemplateRequest.description:
New wording for a template. `name` renames the organization's own template; leave it out for a built-in,
whose name is ScreenHire's.

UpdateHiddenViewsRequest.description: Replaces the built-in views the member hides; each id once.

UpdateJobRequest.description:
Replaces a job's posting content. A published job keeps its slug; a closed job cannot change. The description is rich
text, as on CreateJobRequest. A blank or missing summary goes back to following the description.

UpdateJobWorkflowRequest.description:
Replaces a job's workflow with the recruiter's edit of it: the job's own copy, tailored. `expectedWorkflowVersion`
is the `workflowVersion` the edit started from; if someone saved in between, the request is refused (409) rather
than overwriting their change. A stage that still holds applications cannot be removed.

UpdateNotificationSettingsRequest.description: Replaces the signed-in member's notification settings; `off` names each kind at most once.

UpdateOrganizationRequest.description:
Renames the organization and, when given, sets its questions per page (1 to 50); null keeps it. Its slug, and so its
careers address, stays as it is.

UpdateRetentionRequest.description: Sets the period (1 to 120 months), or turns retention off with `null`.

UpdateRoleRequest.description: Renames a custom role and sets what it can do.

UpdateScorecardTemplateRequest.description: An own scorecard's name and questions, replaced whole. Jobs that copied it keep their copy.

UpdateSlackAccountRequest.description: Whether mentions and tasks given to the member arrive as direct messages.

UpdateSlackChannelRequest.description: The channel to post to, by its id from the channel list, and the events posted there (none is allowed).

UpdateVerificationSettingsRequest.description:
Replaces the organization's verification settings. `apiKey` is the one place a key travels: null keeps the saved key,
text replaces it. Changing the provider or the address needs a new key, and a change to the key, provider, address or
model is tested before it is saved. `modelSource` `Included` erases the saved key, provider and price fields.
A preset with a fixed address takes no `baseUrl`. The monthly budget and cap are not here: an Owner sets them with
`/v1/organization/ai-usage/limits`.

UpdateViewRequest.description: Renames a view, shares it or makes it private; a member left out stays as it is.

UpdateWebhookEndpointRequest.description:
Replaces an endpoint's settings. A body without `enabled` keeps the endpoint on or off as it is. Turning it
back on clears an automatic disable and its failure count; deliveries skipped while it was off stay skipped and can
be replayed.

UploadedFile.description: An upload that was found and checked. Its `uploadId` is the answer to its file question.

UploadRequest.description: Asks for a link to upload one file for a file question. `sizeBytes` is the size the candidate's device reports.

UploadTicket.description:
Where and how to upload one file, and until when: send its bytes with `method` to `uploadUrl` with
`headers`, then refer to it by `uploadId`.

UsageItem.description:
One thing that uses a template. `id` is the job's or the hiring template's id; for an automation it is the job
or template the automation belongs to, and `automationId` and `automationName` name the automation.

UsageKind.description: What uses a template: a job, a hiring template, or an automation in either.

UsageUnit.description: What a monthly budget or cap is counted in.

ValidateWorkflowRequest.description: A workflow to check, as the builder holds it before saving.

VerificationActionAvailability.description: Whether an action is offered, and why not when it is not.

VerificationAlerts.description: The two notifications and the channels each goes to. Slack messages are direct messages to the people who can act.

VerificationChecks.description: Which groups of checks run. A group that is off is recorded on each result it would have contributed to.

VerificationDismissal.description: A reviewer set an assessment aside. `actorName` is the reviewer's display name, when they have one.

VerificationMatches.description:
Applications whose current verification matches a level filter, for a key with the Verification read scope. Each is a
pointer to read in full (`GET /v1/applications/{id}/verification`), not a ranking: the order is newest first and a
level is evidence for a person to review, never a reason to reject on its own (ADR-0004).

VerificationModelList.description:
The models the provider lists for the key. `listed` is false when it offers no list or could not be asked; type
the model id then.

VerificationModelRequest.description:
An own-key endpoint to list models for or test. A null `apiKey` uses the saved key when `provider` and
`baseUrl` match what is saved, so the page never needs the key back. `model` is needed to test.

VerificationModelTest.description: Whether the endpoint answered a tiny request with the key and model. `problem` is a word, never the provider's text.

VerificationReasonExplanation.description: A reviewer marked one reason explained. `actorName` is the reviewer's display name, when they have one.

VerificationReviewEntry.description: One entry of the verification audit log, oldest first.

VerificationSignalView.description:
One signal, renderable by its evidence kinds alone (`evidence[].kind`). Weight and confidence are categories,
not numbers.

VerificationSummary.description:
The verification chips for an application in a list: each current level and its reason codes (shown as "3 reasons"), and
whether a reviewer dismissed it. Null on the summary until the application is assessed.

ViewFilters.description:
What a view filters and how it sorts. `baseView` is a built-in view this one narrows; `jobIds` and
`stages` pick jobs and stages (stage names on the Candidates page, stage ids on a job's table); `authenticity`
is an authenticity level name or `Pending`; `aiAssistance` an AI assistance level name; `sortColumn` the
sorted column, or none for the table's own order. Search text is not saved.

ViewList.description: The views the member sees, oldest first, and the ids of the built-in views they hid.

ViewScope.description: Which table a view filters: the Candidates page, or one job's candidates.

WebhookDeliveryEntry.description:
One delivery in an endpoint's log. string WebhookDeliveryEntry.Payload is the exact body sent; Guid? WebhookDeliveryEntry.ReplayOfId is set on
a replay. string? WebhookDeliveryEntry.LastError is our description of the last failed attempt, never the receiver's response.

WebhookEndpointEntry.description:
One webhook endpoint. The signing secret is never part of it: it appears once, in the create and rotate responses.
string? WebhookEndpointEntry.DisabledReason says why the worker turned the endpoint off, when it did.

WebhookEndpointWithSecret.description:
An endpoint with its signing secret, returned only when the secret is new (create, rotate). Store it now: the API
cannot show it again. Check each delivery's `ScreenHire-Signature: t={unix seconds},v1={hex}`, the hex
HMAC-SHA256 of `{t}.{raw body}` keyed with this secret.

WorkflowChange.description: One difference between two workflows. `before` and `after` are values, or JSON for objects and lists.

WorkflowStage.description: One step of the pipeline. `hired`, `rejected` and `withdrawn` are terminal.

WorkflowValidationResult.description:
The validator's verdict, guardrails included. 200 either way: a workflow with problems is a normal answer here, and
each problem has a JSON path such as `automations[0].actions[0]` the builder can point at.

session.description: The dashboard's session, from signing in. Changes also need the X-XSRF-TOKEN header.
session.name: sh.session

apiKey.description: An organization API key, created by an owner or admin. Works on jobs, applications, candidates, templates and reports, and, with the VerificationRead scope an owner gives it, on verification results.
